description: This topic is a crucial component of quantitative aptitude based on the principles of Time and Work. It involves analyzing the rates at which inlet and outlet pipes fill or empty a reservoir or tank to determine the total time required for various operations.

sections.title: Fundamental Concepts
sections.description: Basic terminology and core principles related to pipes and cisterns.

key_concepts.explanation: A pipe connected to a tank that fills it with water. The work done by an inlet pipe is always considered positive work.
A pipe or leak that empties water from a filled or partially filled tank. The work done by an outlet pipe is always considered negative work.

sections.title: Basic Formulas and Calculation
sections.description: Fundamental mathematical rules for calculating unit work and efficiency.

equations: If an inlet pipe can fill a tank in x hours, the part filled in 1 hour = 1/x
If an outlet pipe can empty a tank in y hours, the part emptied in 1 hour = 1/y

sections.title: Important Standard Cases
sections.description: Direct results and formulas for specific scenarios involving multiple pipes operating simultaneously.

cases.condition: When two inlet pipes A and B can independently fill a tank in x and y hours respectively.
results: Total time taken to fill the tank together = (xy) / (x + y) hours

cases.condition: When one inlet pipe fills the tank in x hours and one outlet pipe empties it in y hours, where y > x (meaning the inlet pipe is faster).
results: Total time taken to fill the tank = (xy) / (y - x) hours

cases.condition: When one inlet pipe fills the tank in x hours and one outlet pipe empties it in y hours, where x > y (meaning the outlet pipe is faster).
results: Total time taken to empty the full tank = (xy) / (x - y) hours

sections.title: The LCM / Efficiency Method
sections.description: A step-by-step strategy for solving complex problems rapidly without relying heavily on fractions.

steps.title: Assume Total Capacity
steps.detail: Find the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of all the given individual times and assume this value as the total capacity (total work) of the tank in units.

steps.title: Calculate Individual Efficiency
steps.detail: Divide the total capacity by the time taken by each respective pipe to find their per-hour efficiency (units filled or emptied per hour).

steps.title: Assign Algebraic Signs
steps.detail: Assign a positive (+) sign to the efficiency of inlet pipes and a negative (-) sign to the efficiency of outlet pipes or leaks.

steps.title: Find Final Time
steps.detail: Calculate the net efficiency by adding the signed efficiencies. The total time required is equal to Total Capacity divided by Net Efficiency.

sections.title: Alternate Operation Strategy
sections.description: A methodical approach for scenarios where pipes are opened one after the other in alternate hours.

steps.title: Identify the Cycle Work
steps.detail: Calculate the net work done in one complete cycle of operation (e.g., the net units filled in a 2-hour period if two pipes operate alternately).

steps.title: Approach Total Capacity
steps.detail: Multiply the cycle work by the largest integer that keeps the total work just below or equal to the total capacity without exceeding it.

steps.title: Calculate Remaining Work
steps.detail: Determine the remaining units of work and divide this by the efficiency of the pipe whose turn it is next. Add this fractional time to the time taken by the full cycles to get the final answer.
